dev_notes: Two semantics on purpose: the PDF always diffs against its own predecessor, however old, while the Markdown docs tag New and Changed only while the target release is still in progress, so a shipped release's docs read as a clean present-tense list. Nothing is tagged by hand. The third register is the `backfilled` flag on a history entry, set by --backfilled on add/update/remove; it wins over new and updated in the badge derivation, and its wording is overridable under docs.tags in config.json. Nothing is ever written into a past release, so an already-issued edition still reprints unchanged.

history.name: New and changed highlighting
history.description: Every edition marks its own changes against the edition before it: a green stripe for a feature that is new, a blue stripe and a "What changed" note for one that was reworked, and no stripe for an entry that stands as it did. The front page counts how many of each. A first edition has nothing behind it to compare against, so it prints as a plain inventory with no stripes anywhere on it.

Every edition marks its own changes against the edition before it: a green stripe for a feature that is new, a blue stripe and a "What changed" note for one that was reworked, a grey stripe marked Already in place for one that was already part of the product and appears in the ledger for the first time, and no stripe for an entry that stands as it did. The front page counts how many of each. A first edition has nothing behind it to compare against, so it prints as a plain inventory with no stripes anywhere on it.
